novelty.reasoning: Core claim is the stale/lagging uncertainty account: reflection is triggered by an outdated gating-uncertainty signal that lags a fresher evidence-uncertainty signal, and an uncertainty-refresh patch can break the loop. That is a real delta from prior confidence-gating/early-exit/steering work, which largely assumes the internal confidence is current. However, the idea is still tightly adjacent to active 2025-26 work on uncertainty during reasoning, so the novelty is mainly in the temporal-lag mechanism and intervention, not a new task or theory family.
revision_notes: State the exact falsifiable distinction from prior confidence-gating papers: not uncertainty exists, but the gating probe is temporally lagged relative to the freshest-state probe.
Add one sentence explaining why this is not just another calibration/early-exit result, but a temporal-update failure claim.
Clarify the novelty of uncertainty refresh as a mechanism: what is patched, at what layer/time, and why prior steering methods cannot reproduce it.
Preempt the main alternative interpretation: reflection as deliberate search/exploration rather than stale confidence.

impact.reasoning: Who cares: interpretability, inference efficiency, and calibration researchers, plus anyone deploying reasoning models at scale. The problem is important because wasted tokens and unnecessary reflection cost latency/money and can degrade user experience. Strongest one-line case: if overthinking is caused by stale confidence, then we can diagnose and fix a common failure mode of reasoning models with a simple intervention. Still, this is somewhat niche and method-adjacent; the real-world reach is more about improving reasoning model efficiency than changing a broad application domain.
revision_notes: Lead with the problem impact, not the probe design: wasted reasoning tokens, latency, and unnecessary compute in deployed reasoning models.
Quantify the operational consequence you care about most: token savings, wall-clock latency, and cost per solved query.
Explain who adopts this if true: model builders using reasoning models at scale, not just interpretability researchers.
Add a concrete downstream scenario where stale uncertainty matters (e.g., long-form math/agentic search) to strengthen the so-what test.

review.reasoning: The hypothesis is plausible and testable, but the proposal has several exposure points. The main logical gap is whether the two uncertainty signals are genuinely separable or just artifacts of read position / probe placement. The causal story from lag to wasted tokens also needs stronger controls against the alternative that continued reflection is intentional exploration. The experimental plan is reasonably feasible, but the current design depends heavily on probe quality and temporal alignment assumptions. Venue-wise, this could be decent if the lag claim and intervention are nailed down; otherwise it risks reading as a post-hoc analysis of known confidence-gating phenomena.
revision_notes: Define the signals more precisely: what exact token/state constitutes gating-uncertainty versus evidence-uncertainty.
Add a preregisterable hypothesis with a directional, falsifiable prediction: lag should increase wasted tokens beyond absolute uncertainty and length under matched correctness.
Include stronger controls for the read-position confound: matched-layer probes, shuffled-time baselines, and identical probe architectures.
Test the exploration alternative directly: tasks where further reflection should help vs tasks where it should not, and compare whether lag still predicts waste.
Add ablations on probe noise/separability: calibration of each probe, inter-run stability, and whether results hold across model families/layers.
Specify minimal viable success criteria if the full refresh patch is too brittle: e.g., diagnostic lag signal alone plus one robust intervention benchmark.
